jobs.title: Vice President, Investment Banking – Biopharma/Life Sciences
jobs.description:
We are passionate about our business and our culture, and are seeking individuals with that same drive.

About Moelis
Moelis & Company (“Moelis”) is a leading global independent investment bank that provides innovative strategic advice and solutions to a diverse client base, including corporations, governments, and financial sponsors. The Firm assists its clients in achieving their strategic goals by offering comprehensive integrated financial advisory services across all major industry sectors. Moelis’s experienced professionals advise clients on their most critical decisions, including mergers and acquisitions, recapitalizations and restructurings, capital markets transactions, secondary transactions and primary fundraising, and other corporate finance matters. The Firm serves clients from locations across North and South America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. For further information, please visit: www.moelis.com .

The Opportunity
We are seeking a Vice President to join our Life Sciences team in New York in a science-led seat. This is a role for a dealmaker whose edge is scientific and clinical judgement: you will be a core member of the team who reads the data, forms a view on an asset, and translates that view into valuation, positioning and transaction strategy. You will work alongside execution bankers on biopharma M&A, licensing and partnering, private and public financings, and strategic advisory mandates, and directly with Executive Directors and Managing Directors on client dialogue and origination. To learn more about our recent transactions, please visit: recent transactions

Responsibilities
- Lead scientific and clinical diligence on assets and platforms, including mechanism of action, target validation, clinical data assessment, development risk and probability of success, competitive landscape and differentiation

- Translate scientific judgement into commercial and valuation outputs, including risk-adjusted NPV and rNPV models, peak sales and patient-based forecasts, discounted cash flow, comparable company and precedent transaction analysis, and deal structures including milestones and royalties

- Own the scientific narrative in client and investor materials, and present it credibly to boards, management teams, sponsors and institutional investors

- Support M&A, licensing and partnering, and financing mandates end to end, from target and partner identification through diligence, negotiation support and closing

- Track the therapeutic and modality landscape, clinical and regulatory catalysts, competitor pipelines, deal comparables and financing markets, and convert that into origination ideas for the team

- Partner with execution bankers and capital markets colleagues, and lead, review and develop Analysts and Associates on the deal team

- Contribute to business development and relationship building with biopharma corporate development teams, venture and crossover investors and academic and translational partners

Preferred Qualifications
- 5+ years of relevant experience within biopharma investment banking, equity research, corporate or business development and licensing, life sciences strategy consulting, or venture and crossover investing

- Deep scientific fluency in one or more therapeutic areas or modalities, and the ability to read and interrogate clinical data independently

- Demonstrated ability to build and defend asset-level valuation and forecasting models, including rNPV

- Experience leading and developing deal teams or project teams, and owning the quality of the output

- Credibility and presence with scientific and commercial audiences, from R&D leadership to boards and investors

- Demonstrated maturity, attention to detail, initiative and problem-solving skills, and the ability to adapt to changing client and firm needs

Education
- Advanced degree in the life sciences (PhD, MD, PharmD or MS) or an MBA.

Expected Salary
$250,000 USD

jobs.title: Associate, Investment Banking - Private Capital Advisory (Primaries)
jobs.description:
We are passionate about our business and our culture, and are seeking individuals with that same drive.

Overview
Moelis Private Capital Advisory ("PCA") is a global business providing strategic advisory and distribution to private fund sponsors and institutional investors, spanning primary fundraising, tailored capital raise solutions, and secondary market advisory. Combined with the Firm's financial sponsor franchise, sector expertise and M&A capabilities, PCA delivers customized solutions across strategies including buyout, growth, real assets, special situations and sector-specific strategies.

The Primaries team within Moelis Private Capital Advisory is a leading capital raiser and strategic advisor to global alternative investment managers, advising general partners on the launch and execution of new fund vehicles — flagship and successor funds, first-time funds, separately managed accounts, and co-investment and fundless-sponsor vehicles — across strategies including buyout, growth equity, venture, distressed/turnaround, infrastructure, mezzanine, credit, and real assets. The team positions the fund, builds the LP order book, and runs the process through to final close, working closely with industry and product groups across Moelis and maintaining deep relationships with institutional LPs globally, including pension plans, endowments, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, and funds-of-funds.

Position Description:
The Associate position at Moelis offers exposure to all aspects of a live primary fundraise — from initial mandate evaluation and GP due diligence through final close. The Associate takes on greater ownership of client and LP relationships than the Analyst role, working closely with senior professionals firmwide to help drive process and deliver advice to fund manager clients.

Responsibilities:
- Help drive GP evaluation / due diligence workstreams — assessing the manager's investment portfolio, track record, investment strategy, and quality of the management team — and translate findings into fund positioning

- Oversee preparation of fund marketing materials (investor presentations, PPMs, DDQs, data books, and other data room materials) and review fund economics (management fee, carry, GP commitment, key-person and other LPA terms) for accuracy and market positioning

- Manage investor roadshows and day-to-day GP client support through soft-circling, first close, subsequent closes, and final close

- Own the data room and documentation flow for active fundraising campaigns, coordinating with GP counsel and fund administrators as needed

- Work directly with senior distribution/sales bankers to track investor feedback, manage the LP demand schedule / status report, and report on fundraising pipeline

- Manage LP due diligence, including responses to DDQs and coordination on necessary follow-up items to drive towards a commitment

- Supervise Analysts on databases of active and historical fund closings, fund terms and benchmarks, and institutional LP investors (profiles, allocation strategies, and preferences)

- Serve as a primary point of contact for institutional investors (pension plans, endowments and foundations, SWFs, insurance firms, funds-of-funds, family offices, asset managers, etc.) throughout the fundraise

- Conduct and oversee primary market research, including fundraising volumes, fund terms, and LP allocation trends across the alternatives industry

- Support business development by identifying new GP fundraising mandates and opportunities across the private capital markets

Qualifications:
Candidates for the Associate position should exhibit a strong history of academic achievement as well as possess the following attributes:
- 3-5 years of relevant experience in investment banking, private equity, primary fund placement, or fund of funds, with direct transaction exposure

- Strong understanding of the private equity industry and primary fundraising market

- Highly motivated individual with a strong desire to learn

- Keen attention to detail

- Strong analytical and technical skills (including extensive experience with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word and CRMs such as Salesforce or DealCloud)

- Ability to think creatively in order to solve problems and effectively market fund strategies

- Excellent communication skills

- Organized, with good judgment and time management skills

- Ability to work independently and as part of a broader team, with the ability to manage and mentor junior team members

Compensation Expectations:  USD $175,000 – $225,000

jobs.title: Associate, Investment Banking - Technology - London
jobs.description:
We are passionate about our business and our culture, and are seeking individuals with that same drive.
About Moelis & Company

Moelis & Company is a leading global independent investment bank that provides innovative strategic advice and solutions to a diverse client base, including corporations, governments and financial sponsors.  The Firm assists its clients in achieving their strategic goals by offering comprehensive integrated financial advisory services across all major industry sectors.  Moelis & Company’s experienced professionals advise clients on their most critical decisions, including mergers and acquisitions, recapitalizations and restructurings, capital markets transactions, and other corporate finance matters.  The Firm serves its clients from 23 geographic locations in North and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia

Overview of the Technology Team

Moelis & Company’s Technology investment banking team is a dedicated sector group advising leading technology, media and telecom (TMT) companies and — in particular — the financial sponsors that own them, across the US, UK, Europe and globally. The team works as part of the Firm’s global Technology franchise, with a core focus on sponsor-led sell-side M&A processes and technology capital markets.

Our mandate is predominantly financial-sponsor M&A — sponsor-to-sponsor sales, public-to-private situations, and minority & growth investments, complemented by strategic advisory and advice on continuation vehicles/financing.  Sector coverage spans across the Technology landscape including horizontal & vertical software and data & analytics.

At Moelis, we foster a client-centric, entrepreneurial environment that empowers Associates to assume early responsibility, engage directly with senior bankers and financial sponsor clients, and contribute meaningfully to high-profile technology transactions.

Position Description:

We are seeking an Associate to join our Technology investment banking team. This role is suited to a high-performing banker with prior technology / TMT M&A experience — ideally on sponsor-led sell-side processes — strong analytical and execution capabilities, and a genuine interest in the technology sector. The Associate will play a key role in the execution of sell-side mandates and financing transactions, financial sponsor coverage, and business development across the team’s technology franchise.

Responsibilities:

- Perform detailed quantitative and qualitative financial analysis, including valuation work (DCF, LBO, public comparable companies, and precedent transactions) and software/SaaS-specific analyses (ARR build, cohort and retention, net revenue retention, and Rule-of-40).
- Develop and maintain complex three-statement operating models and LBO / sponsor returns models to support transaction evaluation and client decision-making.
- Lead the preparation of sell-side marketing materials, including information memoranda (CIMs), management presentations, teasers, sponsor / investment-committee materials, and pitch books.
- Conduct company, industry, and market research to identify actionable sell-side opportunities, acquisition targets, and strategic trends for financial sponsor and corporate clients across the technology landscape.
- Support senior team members across all aspects of transaction execution, including due diligence coordination (VDD, virtual data room, and buyer Q&A), process management, and liaison with clients, sponsors, and external advisors.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with financial sponsors, founders, and management teams through responsiveness, attention to detail, and a deep understanding of client objectives.
- Mentor and supervise analysts, assigning and reviewing workstreams to ensure quality and adherence to deadlines.
- Contribute to business development through idea generation, sponsor and sector mapping, and preparation of client-ready materials.

Qualifications and Experience

- Strong analytical, financial modelling, and presentation skills.
- Solid understanding of accounting, corporate finance, and valuation methodologies, including software / SaaS and other technology operating metrics.
- Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in investment banking (technology / TMT M&A or corporate finance); experience at a sponsor-focused or sell-side advisory practice, or in technology-focused private equity, is particularly relevant.
- Direct sector experience in technology is strongly preferred — across software (vertical and horizontal application software) and / or data & analytics an advantage.
- Demonstrable execution experience on at least 4–6 technology transactions, with a focus on sponsor-led sell-side M&A, of which a minimum of 2–3 should have reached signing or completion; prior experience working with or advising financial sponsors is essential.
- Demonstrated client-focused mindset with the ability to deliver high-quality, tailored solutions.
- Proven team player with excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, detail-oriented, and collaborative environment.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
- Fluency in English is required; proficiency in an additional European language is advantageous.

We seek to ensure that we recruit from a diverse talent pool and that all applicants are treated fairly at each stage of the recruitment process. Summary of Role

The Financial Sponsors Analyst will sit at the centre of Moelis’ European Financial Sponsor Coverage, supporting senior bankers in the development of sponsor relationships, origination of transaction opportunities and coordination of sponsor-related activity across the European platform. The role combines analytical work, market intelligence, materials production and internal process management, providing a differentiated opportunity to develop deep exposure to private equity clients, portfolio company activity and sponsor-led transaction origination.

Reporting to

Managing Director alongside broader senior members of the European Financial Sponsor team. Working pattern is expected to align with team demands, transaction activity and the pace of sponsor coverage.

Key Stakeholders

The Analyst will work closely with:
- European Financial Sponsors bankers across all levels

- Industry and product teams across the European platform

- Senior bankers involved in sponsor coverage, origination and execution

- Internal teams responsible for client data, transaction tracking and business development infrastructure

Detail of Role

The Analyst will support Moelis’ European Financial Sponsors franchise across sponsor coverage, origination and business development, working closely with senior bankers and sector / product teams across the European platform.

Core responsibilities will include:

- Supporting senior bankers in identifying, prioritising and tracking sponsor-related opportunities across sectors, geographies and transaction types

- Preparing high-quality sponsor materials, including credentials, meeting packs, market updates, portfolio company analysis and thematic origination content

- Conducting research and analysis on financial sponsors, portfolio companies, investment themes, adviser usage and transaction activity

- Coordinating with sponsor coverage, industry and product teams to support consistent relationship management and opportunity development

- Supporting preparation for sponsor meetings and selected client-facing interactions, with external exposure expected to increase over time

The role is expected to be predominantly internal initially, requiring strong attention to detail, analytical capability and process discipline. Over time, the Analyst will have the opportunity to develop increased exposure to sponsor clients and portfolio company situations.

Key Measurements of Success

- Quality, accuracy, and timeliness of analytical work, materials and internal outputs

- Effectiveness in supporting origination efforts through data, insights, and execution support

- Strength of internal coordination and information flow across teams

- Reliability and ability to manage multiple workstreams under pressure

- Progression toward increased responsibility and client exposure over time

Qualifications

jobs.description:
We are passionate about our business and our culture, and are seeking individuals with that same drive.

About the Group
Moelis & Company’s Capital Markets Group structures and executes customized financing solutions and advises clients on all aspects of public and private debt and equity transactions. The Group provides independent, objective financing advice across a broad range of situations, including buyouts, growth capital, platform formation, refinancings, restructurings, recapitalizations, project financing, public company financings, and IPOs.

Across public and private transactions, the Group advises clients on preparation, positioning, valuation, investor messaging, and end-to-end execution of the financing process. Our independence and objectivity, coupled with direct and long-standing institutional buy-side relationships, inform our market views and strengthen the quality of our execution, leading to successful transactions for our clients.

Representative product areas include:
- Debt products:   ABL, public and private term loans / unitranche, DIP / exit financing, investment grade debt, high yield bonds, mezzanine debt, and other bespoke credit solutions
- Equity and equity-linked products:  IPOs, convertible debt, structured equity, preferred equity, PIPEs, corporate and portfolio company recapitalizations, follow-on and public company financings, and Board of Directors advisory

The Group maintains direct dialogue with a wide range of institutional investors, including private equity sponsors, venture capital firms, hedge funds, alternative asset managers, bank and non-bank lenders, sovereign wealth and pension funds, family offices, and other capital providers, to ensure the appropriate capital pool can be accessed for our clients.

- Deal coordination:   Serve as a key point of contact across clients, investors / lenders, senior bankers, legal counsel and other parties; manage timelines and deliverables through closing
- Team leadership:   Direct and review Analyst work, ensuring high-quality output while interacting regularly with senior bankers, clients, and external stakeholders

- Familiarity with institutional investors and lenders, including private equity, credit funds, hedge funds, banks, and alternative asset managers
- Ability to produce accurate, high-quality work under tight deadlines and in high-pressure environments
- Strong judgment, intellectual curiosity, attention to detail, and problem-solving skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to interact effectively with internal teams, clients, investors, and other external parties

- Exceptional Excel and PowerPoint skills; strong ability to analyze financial statements and market data; familiarity with market data and research tools such as Bloomberg, Capital IQ, FactSet, Dealogic, or similar platforms

jobs.description:
We are passionate about our business and our culture, and are seeking individuals with that same drive.

Your application will not be considered if you have not completed the Suited assessment and shared your score with Moelis. Additional information about the assessment below. This is a requirement for the application process.

Moelis has partnered with the screening platform   Suited to help us better understand our applicants. Suited uses assessments to holistically and objectively understand what makes you unique. In addition to your academic background and experience, the traits and competencies captured by these assessments are predictive of on-the-job success, while reducing bias in the screening process.

Complete the  Suited assessment here.

To learn more about the assessments, please visit:  Resource Guide for Investment Banking Candidates

We are currently seeking an experienced Analyst to join our Healthcare Life Sciences financial advisory practice in San Francisco.

Moelis & Company Analysts are expected to assume significant levels of responsibility requiring intellectual curiosity, motivation and analytical aptitude. Day-to-day responsibilities of an Analyst include: financial analysis and modeling, company and industry research, preparing client presentations and interacting with senior bankers and clients.

Primary Responsibilities:
- Supports senior managers in origination activities including (but not limited to): preparing historical and projected financial statements, provide analysis of financial implications of mergers and acquisitions and conducting public & private valuation analysis for major corporations

- Involved in execution activities, including basic responsibilities such as data gathering, analysis and material preparation, as well as taking responsibility for managing standard processes such as preparing deal documentation

- Builds and applies valuation models based on financial research & analysis including comparable company analysis, discounted cash flow analysis and comparable acquisitions analysis

- Prepares analytical materials to support necessary credit, compliance, engagement committee and balance sheet approvals

- Conducts corporate operations reviews, portfolio analytic reviews and prepare risk/return valuations

- Gathers and processes market share data and shareholder and investor profile

Required Skills & Experience:
- Results driven and able to perform well under pressure and against tight deadlines

- Strong analytical and numerical skills that put you at ease with financial data

- Proven team player who is able to effectively interact with a wide variety of internal groups and clients

- Strong multi-tasking skills

- Strong Microsoft Office suite (Excel a must) and financial reporting skills

Education:
- Undergraduate degree; focus in finance, business, accounting, economics, mathematics is preferred

Salary Expectations: $110,000 - $135,000
